subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Wide Sargasso Sea and Reclaimed Voice
description: One-minute skill: Wide Sargasso Sea and Reclaimed Voice.

hook.text: In Jane Eyre, the madwoman in the attic had no voice. Jean Rhys decided to give her one.

buildup.text: Wide Sargasso Sea told the backstory of Bertha Mason as Antoinette, a Creole woman in the Caribbean.

discovery.text: Published in 1966, it revealed how colonialism and patriarchy drove Antoinette to madness and silence.

twist.text: Rhys exposed that Charlotte Brontë's classic heroine triumphed only by erasing a colonized woman's story.

climax.text: The novel pioneered postcolonial literature by rewriting a Western classic from the margins.

punchline.text: The silent woman in the attic finally told her story.

quiz.question: What did Wide Sargasso Sea do to Jane Eyre?
options: It continued the story after Jane Eyre's ending
It gave voice to Bertha Mason, the silenced madwoman in the attic
It translated Jane Eyre into French
